Hi Simon / Olivia,

Thanks again for the call today — good to meet the HealthPay security and engineering leads. Quick recap and the items we agreed to follow up on so we keep momentum for the POC: 

1) SOC 2 / compliance posture
   - You asked whether we’re SOC 2 Type II and what the scope covers. Short answer: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II (security + availability controls in scope) — I will attach our attestation and the scope map in the follow-up.

2) Data residency & GDPR/HIPAA
   - We confirmed you need EU data residency for EU customers and HIPAA coverage for PHI processing in the US. For the POC we can pin to an EU region (GCP europe-west) and enable our HIPAA support plan for US-based PHI.

3) Subprocessor / third-party mapping
   - You asked for our subprocessor list and to know what cloud providers and SaaS vendors handle customer data (logs, metrics, backups). Action: I’ll send a high-level subprocessor CSV and call out data boundaries.

4) Vendor security questionnaire
   - You indicated you’ll send a short questionnaire. We’re happy to accept the spreadsheet or complete a DocuSign-secured vendor form.

Next steps I’ll take:
- Attach SOC 2 attestation & scope map (attachment).
- Attach preliminary subprocessor list (high level) and follow up with Marissa for the full CSV.
- Confirm region options and HIPAA setup steps in a separate note.

Can you share the security questionnaire when ready (or point me at the DocuSign/SharePoint link)? Also confirm whether you want the subprocessor list redacted (some customers request limited vendor contact details).

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni

Simon / Vivek / team —

Attached is the subprocessor export CSV (redwood_subprocessor_list_2026-11.csv). Key callouts below to help map to your questionnaire: 

Summary (top-level):
- SOC 2 Type II: our attestation covers the production serving stack (inference runtime, control plane, deployment orchestration) and monitoring/alerting. It does not cover customer-managed on-prem packages once deployed to a customer VPC.
- Encryption at rest: YES. We encrypt customer data at rest using AES-256. For hosted deployments we use cloud KMS options (AWS KMS, GCP KMS); for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key).
- Backups & geo-location: For accounts pinned to EU regions we keep backups within the selected region by default. Cross-region backup replication is configurable; we do not replicate EU-resident backups to non-EU locations unless explicitly requested and documented in the MSA.
- Logging/telemetry: Our telemetry pipeline collects anonymized metrics by default. The default logging does NOT capture full customer request payloads. We retain request traces and minimal sampling for debugging; raw requests are only captured if a customer enables full request logging for support, and that is documented and requires customer approval.

Subprocessor highlights (see CSV for full list):
- Cloud compute & storage: AWS (us-east-1, eu-west-1) and GCP (europe-west1) — handle model serving and persistent storage (only metadata/artefacts for EU accounts unless customer opts in to shared infra).
- Caching & KV: RedisLabs (managed Redis) — stores ephemeral KV caches; does not store long-term PII.
- Observability & logs: Datadog — metrics and alerting (no raw payloads by default).
- Analytics & crash reporting: Sentry (anonymized telemetry).
- Customer emails / support: Zendesk — ticketing data; PII only if customer provides it in support conversations.

Attachments included: redwood_subprocessor_list_2026-11.csv (CSV, internal contact emails redacted per our standard export) and redwood_soc2_scope_map_2026.pdf.

If you prefer, we can complete the XLSX questionnaire directly; otherwise these files plus the short answers above should map to the intake. Happy to jump on a 30-min call with your security team to walk through any controls.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Security & Compliance Program Manager | Redwood Inference
